newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to softer despite crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to softer despite crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to down slightly Wednesday in quiet trade, with ample inventories still weighing on the market despite firmer crude and forecasts for more cold next week, industry sources said.

"Everyone's got barrels. We'll have to see how long the cold lasts," said one cash trader, adding recent utility demand has been slow but some may soon be out looking for barrels, particularly with gas still at a steep premium.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped at least 15 cents to $19.50-75 a barrel, but some pegged the number even lower, traders said.
NYH paper prices continued to erode despite the crude rally, with January reportedly done at sub-$19, then talked in the low-$19 area, off more than 50 cents on the day.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour held relatively steady at $20.75-21.00, with low pour still in the $23.25-50 area.
High sulphurs in New York again were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was a quarter lower at $18.25-50, while three percent was flat at about $16.50.
New York city gate gas prices slipped 20 cents or so to about the $4.30/mmBtu area despite colder East Coast weather. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.12/mmBtu equivalent.
